text: Jean Preudhomme, also known as Preud'ho(m)me or Prudhomme (c. 23 November 1732 – c. 20 July 1795), was a Swiss painter who lived during the same period as other notable Swiss artists such as Anton Graff, Johann Jakob Schalch, Angelica Kauffman, Jakob Emanuel Handmann, Johann Caspar Füssli, and his son Johann Heinrich Füssli. He was baptised on 23 November 1732 in Rolle and studied under the renowned painters Jean Baptiste Le Prince and Jean-Baptiste Greuze in Paris. Specialising in landscape and animal painting, his primary focus was portrait painting. He gained significant popularity among the landed gentry and patricians in Geneva, Lausanne, Neuchâtel, and Bern. A Swiss publication from 1782 to 1786 referred to him as a “portraitist à la mode.” Preudhomme’s works, particularly his portraits, are rare in the art market, with his portrait of Franz Rudolf Frisching being one of his most well-known pieces. His portrait of Douglas, 8th Duke of Hamilton, depicting the Duke on his Grand Tour with his physician Dr John Moore and the latter’s son John, with a view of Geneva in the background, is held in the National Museums of Scotland. During this Grand Tour, the Duke and his companions resided in Geneva for two years. Additionally, a portrait of a Lady is part of the Musée Rath’s collection.
